Updated interpretation incorporating the April 2022 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey (SLOOS):

- Policy stance: Still hawkish. The FOMC raised the funds rate to 0.75–1.00% and will begin balance‑sheet reduction on June 1 to combat elevated inflation.
- FSR risk context (unchanged): Russia–Ukraine and China lockdowns add upside inflation pressure and downside growth/market risks; vulnerabilities in nonbank finance and market liquidity persist; valuations elevated; banks well capitalized.
- SLOOS lending standards and demand:
  - C&I: Domestic banks eased standards and reported stronger demand across working‑capital and capex uses (inventory, A/R, plant, and equipment). Foreign banks, by contrast, tightened some C&I standards.
  - CRE: Standards largely unchanged across construction/land development and nonfarm nonresidential; modest easing for multifamily.
  - Residential real estate: Banks reported weaker mortgage demand.
  - Consumer: Banks eased standards on credit cards; demand strengthened for HELOCs and auto loans.
- Implications: Despite rate hikes, bank credit supply remained accommodative and credit demand was firm at the start of Q2, supporting near‑term spending and investment. This tempers immediate growth downside flagged by the FSR, but it also reinforces the need for continued policy tightening to cool demand and inflation.

Net: Cautiously hawkish. SLOOS shows resilient credit availability and demand, softening the near‑term growth pessimism from the FSR. Overall stance remains negative for risk (inflation risks to the upside, policy tightening ongoing), but less negative than an FSR‑only read.
